answer: A trellis of mutual attestation: newcomers lock a refundable stake and earn signed receipts only from randomly assigned peers who verify real completed work, building a reputation lattice no one can buy in bulk. Forging history is like carving karst caves by hand — each fake receipt costs real stake and time, and one contradiction collapses the chain and slashes the deposit. A gale of fresh throwaway identities carries no weight, because trust accrues only from verified output, and an identity with no history starts at the bottom.
